header.name: Key Concepts in Political Theory
header.description: The course analyses the debates on some of the key political concepts informing the idea of Indian constitutionalism. Even as these concepts are universal; they inhabit political imaginations across the world and are an integral part of every democratic constitution, there are distinctive features to this debate in the Indian context. But concepts as W.B Gallie had argued are always contested, and major debates have erupted around the five concepts in the Preamble: justice, liberty, equality, fraternity, and secularism. Debates in the specific context of India have expanded not only the conceptual universe, but also filled in many of the gaps in predominantly Western debates. Liberty has been articulated as Swaraj, equality includes affirmative action and representation, justice is interpreted as the obligation of the state to provide wellbeing and the right to have rights, fraternity as solidarity with the doubly disadvantaged, and secularism as equality of religions.
